# ankra_application_alert (Resource)

An alert of one application on one of its environments (`ankra application alerts`): it fires when one of the application's own metrics reads above a threshold for a number of minutes in a row, and notifies 1 to 5 alert destinations. The platform stores it as an organisation alert named "Application · Environment · name" with one rule, so it also shows under Alerts, where it can be muted; `enabled` reports that. Every member except `application_id` changes in place. `severity` is `warning` when the alert is created without one, and leaving it out of the configuration later keeps the severity the platform stores rather than resetting it. Destroy deletes the alert and its rule.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Pages on-call when the application's 95th percentile response time on
# production stays above 800 ms for 5 minutes in a row.
resource "ankra_application_alert" "slow_responses" {
  application_id = ankra_application.web.id
  environment_id = var.production_environment_id
  name           = "Slow responses"
  severity       = "critical"

  condition = {
    metric       = "p95_ms"
    threshold    = 800
    hold_minutes = 5
  }

  send_to = [ankra_alert_destination.pagerduty.id]
}

# Without severity the platform stores warning; leaving it out later keeps
# whatever severity the alert has.
resource "ankra_application_alert" "failed_requests" {
  application_id = ankra_application.web.id
  environment_id = var.production_environment_id
  name           = "Failed requests"

  condition = {
    metric       = "failed_share_pct"
    threshold    = 5
    hold_minutes = 10
  }

  send_to = [ankra_alert_destination.platform_channel.id]
}

# `ankra application environments <application>` lists the ids.
variable "production_environment_id" {
  type = string
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `application_id` (String) Identifier of the application. Changing it replaces the alert.
- `condition` (Attributes) When the alert fires: `metric` reads above `threshold` for `hold_minutes` in a row. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--condition))
- `environment_id` (String) Identifier of the application's environment the alert watches; `ankra application environments <application>` lists them. An environment with nothing running on it yet is accepted: the alert reads unknown until something runs there.
- `name` (String) The alert's name on the application page, 1 to 100 characters. Under Alerts it is named "Application · Environment · name", which must be unique in the organisation.
- `send_to` (Set of String) Identifiers of the alert destinations (`ankra_alert_destination`) the alert notifies, 1 to 5.

### Optional

- `severity` (String) `critical`, `warning` or `info`. Unset on create, the platform stores `warning`; unset on a later apply, the platform keeps the severity it stores, including one changed outside Terraform, and the plan shows no change.

### Read-Only

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the alert and its rule are both on. It is `false` while the alert is muted under Alerts.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the alert.
- `rule_id` (String) Identifier of the alert's one rule.

<a id="nestedatt--condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `condition`

Required:

- `hold_minutes` (Number) How many minutes the reading stays above the threshold before the alert fires, 1 to 60.
- `metric` (String) `failed_share_pct` (the share of requests that failed, in percent), `p95_ms` (the 95th percentile response time, in milliseconds) or `restarts` (container restarts in the last 15 minutes).
- `threshold` (Number) The reading the metric must be above, zero or more; at most 100 for `failed_share_pct`.

Optional:

- `condition_type` (String) `app_metric`, the one condition an application alert can have.
- `operator` (String) `gt`, the one operator the platform takes: the alert fires when the reading is above the threshold.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Application alerts are imported by application id and alert id.
terraform import ankra_application_alert.slow_responses 5b0c4a9e-2f43-4b8e-9a51-1f0d8e7c2a10/4c2a9e1f-2222-4333-8444-955556666777
```
